purpose: Fixes #300 (api-data-fetching audit findings) by hardening audit duplicate prevention with a fail-closed existing-issue search, reconstructing review-comment threads from a single paginated pass with a direct-fetch fallback, expanding conversation pagination to a bounded 2000-comment window, adding fail-loud error handling to the autofix flow, propagating failed-batch counts into review results with a 'Partial review' banner, authenticating the opencode release download, wiring AbortSignal through the GitHub/GitLab API helpers, and keying the lessons cache by the file-path set.
riskRationale: The opencode release download now sends ambient tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN / INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN) to api.github.com for a cross-repo release lookup, deterministically breaking the GitLab CI flow (a non-GitHub-scoped token is sent to the GitHub API) and risking 404/403 for repo-scoped GitHub tokens. A thread-reconstruction index bug can duplicate comments into the reply context, the GitLab adapter ignores the asc ordering assumption so threads can be reversed, the audit fail-closed search silently drops issue creation on failure, and none of the new code paths are covered by tests.
breakingChanges: opencode release lookup now authenticates with ambient tokens, which breaks the GitLab CI flow and may break cross-repo release lookups in GitHub Actions

text: The PR is a well-structured reliability hardening pass that fixes a genuine stale-lessons-cache bug, adds fail-loud pagination and abort-signal plumbing, and honestly surfaces partial reviews via failedBatches. However, it introduces a deterministic regression in the opencode download path (breaks GitLab CI), a thread-reconstruction index bug that can duplicate comments in the reply context, a GitLab ordering mismatch that can reverse reconstructed threads, and a silent audit drop on search failure. None of the new logic is covered by tests and pnpm lint currently fails, so the branch needs targeted fixes and added tests before merge.

reasoning: Merge-blocking: the authenticated opencode release fetch deterministically breaks the GitLab CI flow and can 404 cross-repo GitHub release lookups, and the needsDirectWalk fallback (chainIds[chainIds.length - 1] selects the leaf) duplicates in-window ancestors into the reconstructed thread. Both have well-defined, localized fixes and the missing tests are straightforward to add, so an automated agent can address them safely.

message: Keying the lessons cache by the sorted, deduplicated file-path set is a correct bug fix: previously lessons for one file set were reused for any other file set within the 60s TTL, silently serving stale/mismatched learning context. It also aligns the lessons cache with the existing mcpDocsCache pattern.

failedBatches is propagated into the final result and rendered as a prominent 'Partial review' banner in review-body.ts:53, so consumers and the autofix loop can tell findings may be incomplete instead of silently trusting a partial result.

Reconstructing the review-comment thread from a single paginated list (when prNumber is provided) converts an inherently sequential N+1 walk of direct comment fetches into one bounded fetch, retaining the direct walk only as a fallback. The design intent is good even though the fallback has an index bug (see issues).

Abort-signal plumbing through api()/graphql() into withRetry is correct: withRetry checks signal.aborted before each attempt and sleep() rejects on abort, so cancellation terminates promptly rather than continuing to retry a canceled request.
Fail-fast on comment fetch errors with a sanitized setFailed message prevents silently miscounted iteration counts that could bypass maxIterations and cause unbounded autofix loops.
mergePR and enableAutoMerge now log the underlying error instead of silently swallowing it, meaningfully improving debuggability of the autofix pipeline.

setupOpenCode now sends the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN || INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN as an Authorization bearer header to api.github.com for the anomalyco/opencode release lookup. In the GitLab CI flow (.gitlab-ci.yml sets INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN to a non-GitHub-scoped token), that token is sent to the GitHub API and returns 401, deterministically breaking setupOpenCode on any runner where opencode is not pre-installed. In GitHub Actions, the auto-created GITHUB_TOKEN is scoped only to the current repository and returns 403/404 for a cross-repo release endpoint where the previous anonymous request worked.
suggestion: Only send the token when it is known to be GitHub-scoped and authorized for the target repo, and on 401/403/404 retry the lookup anonymously so an auth failure degrades gracefully instead of aborting setup.

message: In the needsDirectWalk fallback of getReviewCommentThread, lastId is taken from chainIds[chainIds.length - 1], which is the LEAF (trigger) comment: the chain is built with unshift while ascending, so ancestors are at the front and the leaf is last. When an ancestor falls outside the paginated window (or a middle page silently fails), the walk starts from the leaf's in_reply_to_id, re-fetches a comment that is ALREADY in commentById, and unshifts it a second time, producing duplicate comment IDs in the returned thread (e.g. [1,2,2,3]). The reply handler feeds this duplicated comment into the LLM prompt, corrupting the conversation context.
suggestion: Start the direct ancestor walk from the deepest already-found ancestor (chainIds[0]), whose in_reply_to_id is the first genuinely missing comment, so in-window comments are never re-fetched or re-added.

message: On a failed existing-issue search (throwOnError after internal withRetry and circuit-breaker attempts are exhausted), the catch block now returns early with only a warning, silently skipping audit issue creation. The audit's critical/important findings are never recorded as an issue and no failure is surfaced (the action exits green) — the opposite failure mode of the duplicate bug being fixed, and a drop that is largely invisible to operators.
suggestion: Retry the search with bounded backoff; if it still fails, surface the abort as a visible failure (core.setFailed) so operators know the audit issue was not tracked, rather than returning quietly.

message: Thread gathering now assumes ascending ordering (direction: 'asc'), which is used for the in_reply_to_id chain, the triggerIdx-5 context slice, and thread ordering. GitLabAdapter.paginate ignores the direction option entirely (it never appends sort/order_by to the URL) and GitLab returns notes newest-first by default. On GitLab the reconstructed review thread is therefore reversed (leaf-first) and the issue-comment context slice picks newer instead of older comments, giving the LLM wrong conversational context.
suggestion: Make GitLabAdapter.paginate honor the direction option (append order_by=created_at and sort), or order the returned items client-side before use, and only rely on the asc assumptions once ordering is guaranteed on both platforms.

message: When the trigger comment is found in the window, threadComments is filtered to only the in_reply_to_id ancestor chain of the trigger. Sibling replies to the same parent/root (a valid GitHub thread tree with multiple branches) are now dropped, losing conversation context that the previous root+direct-replies logic preserved — the rewrite narrows the context the model sees rather than improving it.
suggestion: Include the whole thread subtree: walk from the chain root and include every comment that directly or transitively replies to a comment in the chain (a BFS over in_reply_to_id), then sort ascending by id, so both ancestor and sibling replies reach the engine.

message: The in-window ancestor-chain walk stops silently when a comment's in_reply_to_id is not present in the fetched window: the loop only terminates when rawComments.find(...) returns undefined, and the direct-fetch fallback is gated on the TRIGGER comment being missing, not on an ancestor being missing. A deep thread whose root is older than the window produces a conversation context with the root silently omitted, contradicting the stated intent that the conversation is never silently skipped. This also reimplements thread logic that getReviewCommentThread now provides on the adapter, so the two implementations will drift.
suggestion: After walking the chain, detect when the loop ended because an ancestor was not in rawComments and fetch the missing ancestors by ID (mirroring the needsDirectWalk logic in GitHubHelper.getReviewCommentThread) — ideally by delegating conversation.ts to gh.getReviewCommentThread and mapping its result to ConversationMessage[] so the ancestor-fallback logic is shared and consistent.

message: The chain walk calls rawComments.find(...) inside the while loop, giving O(n*m) worst-case behavior with n up to 2000 comments in the window, and both chain walks loop on in_reply_to_id with no cycle guard. Since in_reply_to_id comes from external API data, a malformed or cyclic chain would hang the webhook handler.
suggestion: Index rawComments into a Map<id, comment> once before walking the chain (as getReviewCommentThread in github.ts already does) and track visited IDs, breaking the loop if a comment id is revisited.

message: In the fallback path (trigger older than the window), diffHunk is never populated even though GET /pulls/comments/{id} returns diff_hunk and the in-window path sets it from triggerComment.diff_hunk. The model loses hunk context for older-thread replies.
suggestion: Capture diff_hunk when direct-fetching chain comments (add diff_hunk to the chain element type) and set diffHunk from the topmost chain element.

message: gatherIssueCommentThread still returns { thread: [] } when the trigger comment is older than the 2000-comment window, with no direct-fetch fallback — the exact class of bug this PR claims to fix for review comments remains for issue comments on PRs with more than 2000 comments.
suggestion: Mirror the review-comment fallback: when the trigger is not found in the window, fetch it by ID via a by-id call and build a minimal thread instead of returning empty.

message: The per-event fetch window for conversation context grew from ~10 comments (1 page) to up to 2000 comments (20 pages x 100). On large or heavily-commented PRs every @mention now triggers up to 20 sequential paginated API requests per event, materially increasing GitHub API rate-limit pressure for a webhook app that can handle many concurrent events.
suggestion: Reduce the window (e.g. perPage 100, maxPages 5) and rely on the direct-fetch fallback, which already handles comments outside the window.

message: getReviewThreads wraps the graphql call in a manual retry-once try/catch, but graphql() already retries internally via withRetry (default maxRetries 3), so a persistent failure now costs up to ~6 attempts with a misleading retrying-once log. More importantly, on the second failure the break exits the pagination loop entirely, so all remaining thread pages are dropped and getBotReviewThreads/getOpenHumanThreads silently operate on partial thread data.
suggestion: Remove the redundant outer retry and let graphql()'s built-in withRetry handle failures; on a final page failure, log a warning naming the PR and mark the thread data as partial (or rethrow when completeness is required).

message: The new signal?: AbortSignal parameter on api()/graphql() (and the matching one in gitlab-adapter.ts) is never passed by any caller — it is dead plumbing that cannot be exercised until a consumer threads a signal through. The internal wiring is correct, but it adds maintenance surface with no consumer (YAGNI).
suggestion: Either thread a real signal from the callers that need cancellation (e.g. webhook handlers with request lifecycle timeouts), or defer the parameter until there is a consumer.

message: Behavior change: the old walk built filePath/lineNumber from the ROOT comment (it overwrote them while walking leaf-to-root), but the new root-first loop ends on the LEAF (trigger) comment, so filePath/lineNumber now reflect the trigger instead of the root. For most threads these are identical, but on rebased diffs or threads spanning lines the reported line can differ, which affects the diff snippet fetched in reply.ts:42.
suggestion: If root anchoring is intended, assign filePath/lineNumber once from the root (first chainIds entry) to preserve prior semantics, and document the choice.

message: No tests were added for any of the new behavior despite the PR claiming automated tests were run: the single-pass getReviewCommentThread(commentId, prNumber) path (including the missing-ancestor needsDirectWalk branch where the duplication bug lives), the conversation.ts thread changes, failedBatches propagation through engine.ts, the audit fail-closed abort, and the paginate throwOnError mode are all untested. Existing tests only exercise the legacy no-prNumber walkChainById path, so the most complex new logic is unprotected.
suggestion: Add unit tests for getReviewCommentThread with a prNumber (in-window, missing-ancestor with no duplicate comment IDs, and out-of-window trigger cases), for engine.ts failedBatches preserved through the dedup branch and rendered by buildReviewBody, for paginate throwOnError in both adapters, and for the audit abort-on-search-failure.

message: pnpm lint fails with Biome formatting errors introduced by this PR (paginate options, core.warning/graphql call formatting at github.ts:1318-1320 and 1569/1577, the opencode.ts fetchWithRetry signature, and platform/adapter.ts getIssueComments signature) despite the PR claiming lint passed — CI would block merge.
suggestion: Run pnpm lint --write (or npx biome check --write .) and re-verify, then update the test plan to reflect the actual verification command.

message: When both failedBatches > 0 and the linter-dedup branch fires, the spread { ...parsed, issues, stats } drops the failedBatches field set moments earlier, so the 'Partial review' banner in buildReviewBody silently disappears despite failed batches.
suggestion: Include failedBatches in the dedup branch's result so the partial-review indicator survives the overwrite.
